claims.text: Greg Short asserts that buying slightly older versions of a desired product and investing in heavy customization yields a result more precisely matched to personal specifications than buying new off-the-shelf, because depreciation on the base asset absorbs most of the modification budget while the customization itself creates a one-of-a-kind outcome unavailable at any retail price point.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
claims.speaker_term: buy slightly older products that I can customize and make exactly my dream car
conditions: High-ticket consumer goods where significant aftermarket customization is possible (vehicles, real estate)
Buyer has sufficient capital to fund both acquisition and modification
claims.mechanism: Depreciation on the older base asset frees capital that is redirected into bespoke modifications, producing a unique end-product that cannot be replicated at retail, thereby extracting more exact-fit value per dollar than a new-stock purchase.
bounded_by: Does not apply to products where depreciation signals unreliable quality (e.g., first-generation technology)
Does not apply when customization costs exceed the depreciation discount

examples.text: Greg Short won a Porsche Cayenne Turbo S auction on Bring a Trailer, then sent it to Euro Wise in North Carolina where it was built into a 700-horsepower off-road vehicle: lifted, fitted with large tires, wrapped in British Racing Green, with full performance and lighting upgrades. The total investment was described as equivalent to a $160,000 custom build. Short frames this as a ski and Aspen-house car, with a matching off-road build in progress.

practices.text: When pursuing a dream-spec vehicle or high-ticket durable good, buy a slightly older model at auction rather than new, then redirect the depreciation savings into bespoke customization to produce an exact-fit result.
Commission purpose-built modifications (performance, aesthetics, utility) rather than settling for an off-the-shelf configuration that only approximates your intended use case.
